title: DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 vs GPT-5.6 Luna on DeepSWE: Cost and Coding
gist: A 900-rollout head-to-head on the 113-task DeepSWE agentic coding benchmark finds GPT-5.6 Luna the better engineer (67.2% vs 53.3% pass@1, 7 of 8 domains, all 5 languages) but DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 six times cheaper at $0.10 per rollout. The actionable finding is that a DeepSeek-first cascade escalating to Luna only on test-suite failure solves 78.9% of tasks at $0.385 each, beating the flagship on both accuracy and cost, and even beating a perfect oracle router.

insights.claim: Running DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 first on DeepSWE and escalating to GPT-5.6 Luna only when the test suite rejects the answer solved 78.9% of tasks at $0.385 per task, versus Luna alone at 67.2% for $0.61 — 11.7 points more accurate and about 37% cheaper.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Two-tier routing, not single-model selection, is the cost-performance frontier for agentic coding; inference spend per solved task can fall sharply without a new frontier model.
insights.quote: Run DeepSeek first and escalate to Luna only when your test suite rejects the answer: 78.9% solved at $0.385 per task.
insights.locator: The portfolio play: why the cascade works anyway

insights.claim: The cheap-first cascade on DeepSWE outperforms a hypothetical perfect one-shot oracle router (78.9% vs 74.3%) because two sequential attempts beat one perfect model pick.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Investment in smarter model-routing classifiers is worth less than investment in verifiable retry loops — a structural argument against router-centric AI middleware startups.
insights.quote: The cascade even beats a perfect one-shot oracle router (74.3%), because two swings beat one perfect pick.
insights.locator: The portfolio play: why the cascade works anyway

insights.claim: Cascade accuracy is identical regardless of which model runs first, but leading with the cheap model costs $0.385 per task versus $0.64 leading with the flagship, making cheap-first a free optimization.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: A one-line ordering change in an agent pipeline cuts inference cost ~40% with zero quality loss — the highest ROI knob available to AI-coding product teams.
insights.quote: Accuracy is identical whichever model leads, but DeepSeek-first is much cheaper ($0.385 vs $0.64), so always lead with the cheap one.
insights.locator: Accuracy is identical whichever model leads

insights.claim: The economic mechanism behind the cascade is that a near-free first stage clears roughly 53% of the task queue at ten cents each, so the flagship's price only ever applies to the hard remainder — and those escalated tasks get a second independent attempt on top.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Frontier-model demand may be less elastic to price than volume suggests: cheap open-weight models absorb the easy half of workloads, compressing paid frontier token volume.
insights.quote: The near-free first stage is the entire trick
insights.locator: The near-free first stage is the entire trick

insights.claim: The authors argue the best use of a cheap open-weight coding model is as a front-end to a flagship rather than as a replacement for it, because the combination buys flagship-beating accuracy below the flagship's own price.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Reframes open-weight models as complements rather than substitutes to closed frontier APIs — bullish for open-weight inference hosts without being bearish on frontier labs.
insights.quote: But the sharpest use of DeepSeek is not as a Luna replacement; it is as a Luna front-end.
insights.locator: What it means

insights.claim: The DeepSeek/Luna pair's combined ceiling is 93.8% of DeepSWE tasks, and the 7 tasks neither model ever solves require a stronger third model rather than better routing.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: There is a hard capability floor orchestration cannot cross, preserving demand for genuinely stronger frontier models at the tail of hard tasks.
insights.quote: the 7 tasks neither ever solves (including gql-incremental-graphql-delivery and bandit-structured-nosec-directives) need a stronger third model, not a better router.
insights.locator: The pair's ceiling is 93.8%

insights.claim: On the 113-task DeepSWE benchmark GPT-5.6 Luna leads DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 on pass@1 by 67.2% to 53.3%, a 14-point absolute gap and roughly 26% relative advantage, and stays ahead at every equal attempt count (81.6 vs 70.1 at k=2, 90.3 vs 80.5 at k=4).
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Open-weight models have not closed the raw agentic-coding capability gap; the gap is now monetized through price, not parity.
insights.quote: On raw solving ability, this is not a close fight.
insights.locator: The DeepSWE scoreboard: pass@1 and pass@k

insights.claim: DeepSeek-V4 Flash's pass@2 on DeepSWE (70.1%) already exceeds GPT-5.6 Luna's single-shot pass@1 (67.2%) at about $0.20 versus $0.61, so with a working verifier two cheap attempts match flagship first-try quality for a third of the cost.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Verification quality, not model quality, becomes the binding constraint — value accrues to test-harness and eval tooling that can pick the winning run.
insights.quote: If a verifier can pick the winning run, the cheap model matches the flagship's first-try quality for a third of the price
insights.locator: But DeepSWE is exactly the kind of workload

insights.claim: Reliability, not just average score, separates the two models: Luna posts 43 solid four-of-four tasks against 11 total walls, while DeepSeek-V4 Flash posts only 23 solid tasks against 22 walls, and Luna's coverage/reliability reads 90.3/74.8% versus DeepSeek's 80.5/66.2%.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Cheap models carry roughly twice the rate of unsolvable-wall tasks, which is the variance a production SLA has to price in.
insights.locator: Appendix: Data Table — Solid (4/4) / walls (0/4)

insights.claim: On the DeepSWE leaderboard of 52 configurations, GPT-5.6 Luna ranks 13th and DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 only 30th, so the cheap model is explicitly mid-pack rather than frontier-adjacent.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Headline 'cheapest on the board' marketing coexists with a middling capability rank — check rank alongside price before standardizing on an open-weight model.
insights.locator: Appendix: Data Table — Leaderboard rank (of 52 configs)

themes.theme: Price per solved task, not per token

insights.claim: DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 costs about $0.10 per DeepSWE rollout against GPT-5.6 Luna's $0.61, roughly a 6x per-rollout gap, making it the cheapest configuration on the entire DeepSWE board.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Agentic coding task costs are now measured in dimes, which changes the unit economics of running coding agents at production scale.
insights.quote: DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 is the cheapest model on the entire DeepSWE board: about ten cents a task!
insights.locator: DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 is the cheapest model

insights.claim: Measured in solves per $100 rather than cost per call, DeepSeek-V4 Flash returns 532 solved DeepSWE tasks against GPT-5.6 Luna's 110 — a 4.8x value edge that is smaller than the 6x raw price gap because of the accuracy deficit.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Solves-per-dollar is the correct procurement metric; headline token prices systematically overstate a weak model's advantage.
insights.quote: At $0.61 a task, Luna returns 110 solves per $100 to DeepSeek's 532: a 4.8x value edge for the cheap model.
insights.locator: Cost comparison: DeepSeek-V4 Flash vs GPT-5.6 Luna pricing

insights.claim: The authors call GPT-5.6 Luna 'genuinely cheap' at $0.61 per long-horizon repo task and the easy default when quality is the priority, implying flagship pricing is no longer the barrier to agentic coding adoption.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: If frontier per-task cost is already trivial relative to engineer time, competition shifts from price to reliability and integration.
insights.quote: At $0.61 a task the flagship is genuinely cheap, and it is the easy default when quality is what you care about.
insights.locator: What it means

themes.theme: Cheap costs wall-clock, not just quality

insights.claim: Contrary to the usual 'flash' branding, DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 is the slower model on DeepSWE — a median 23 minutes and 148 steps versus GPT-5.6 Luna's 16 minutes and 92 — so its edge is money, not latency.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Latency-sensitive interactive coding products cannot treat the cheap model as a drop-in; the savings show up in batch/background workloads only.
insights.quote: DeepSeek's advantage is money, not time.
insights.locator: The one thing the cheap model does not buy you is speed

insights.claim: DeepSeek-V4 Flash burns materially more output to get less far — 104k median output tokens versus Luna's 70k at the same 202k median peak context — grinding through more steps for a lower solve rate.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: The cheap model's price advantage survives despite ~50% more output tokens, meaning its per-token price is even further below the flagship's than the per-task ratio implies.
insights.locator: Appendix: Data Table — Median peak context / output tokens

insights.claim: The authors attribute DeepSeek-V4 Flash's wall-clock disadvantage partly to model newness and expect the gap to shrink as inference engines are tuned for it.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Serving-stack optimization is a near-term source of improvement independent of model retraining — watch inference providers' kernel/engine releases.
insights.quote: That wall-clock gap is partly an artifact of how new the model is; expect it to shrink as inference engines get tuned for it.
insights.locator: That wall-clock gap is partly an artifact

insights.claim: DeepSeek-V4 Flash breaks the repository's existing test suite in only 9% of its DeepSWE failures versus GPT-5.6 Luna's 15%, so the cheaper model damages working code less often when it fails.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Failure mode quality, not just solve rate, determines the human review burden — a cheap model that fails cleanly can be safer to deploy unattended.
insights.quote: When DeepSeek fails, it breaks the repository's existing test suite in only 9% of failures. Luna does so in 15%
insights.locator: Failure modes: DeepSeek fails more gracefully than the flagship

insights.claim: The authors identify a persistent 'GPT-family regression signature' of 15-20% of failures breaking existing tests, observed across Sol and other OpenAI-lineage models, and recommend gating any Luna deployment behind a full regression run.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: A model-family-level behavioral defect implies architectural or training-recipe persistence, and creates recurring demand for regression-gating CI tooling around OpenAI-lineage agents.
insights.quote: the GPT-family regression signature, the same 15 to 20% we see across Sol and the other OpenAI-lineage models
insights.locator: Failure modes: DeepSeek fails more gracefully than the flagship

insights.claim: Both models fail predominantly by near miss rather than catastrophic error (DeepSeek 69%, Luna 66%) with zero infrastructure errors across all 900 rollouts, indicating benchmark failures reflect genuine capability limits rather than harness noise.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Near-miss-dominated failure distributions are exactly what makes retry and cascade strategies pay off, validating the parallel-attempt economics.
insights.locator: Both fail mostly by near miss

themes.theme: Where the cheap model is and isn't usable

insights.claim: Across 8 DeepSWE task domains GPT-5.6 Luna wins 7, with its largest margins in reasoning-heavy work: program analysis (69 vs 33), concurrency and durability (70 vs 38) and language/runtime internals (86 vs 59), roughly 30 points each.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: The capability premium is concentrated in system-invariant reasoning — that is the workload segment where frontier pricing power is defensible.
insights.quote: Everywhere the task demands holding a hard invariant across a whole system, Luna's capability separates.
insights.locator: DeepSeek-V4 Flash vs GPT-5.6 Luna by task domain

insights.claim: DeepSeek-V4 Flash wins exactly one DeepSWE domain — query and config languages, 78 vs 70 — covering SQL builders, window functions, keyset pagination and config parsers, where structured convention-following work suits the cheap model.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Data-tooling and config-heavy workloads can be shifted to open-weight models today at 6x cost savings with no accuracy penalty.
insights.quote: Structured, schema-shaped, convention-following work is where the cheap model is genuinely competitive, even ahead.
insights.locator: DeepSeek holds exactly one domain

insights.claim: DeepSeek-V4 Flash's JavaScript performance collapses to 35 versus Luna's 60 — a 25-point hole and the weakest cell in the entire matchup — while it stays respectable on Rust (55 vs 60) and Go (62 vs 79) and soft on Python (49 vs 65).
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Model choice should be routed by language: JS-heavy shops save nothing by switching, Rust/config-heavy shops capture most of the 6x saving.
insights.quote: If your stack is JS-heavy, the cheap model is a false economy; if it is config, query, or Rust, DeepSeek closes most of the gap.
insights.locator: DeepSeek-V4 Flash vs GPT-5.6 Luna by programming language

insights.claim: Per-task correlation between DeepSeek-V4 Flash and GPT-5.6 Luna is only 0.50, but the diversity is lopsided: they jointly solve 87 tasks, Luna alone solves 15, DeepSeek alone solves just 4, and Luna sweeps four tasks DeepSeek never lands while DeepSeek sweeps none Luna misses.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Ensembling cheap and frontier models for coverage does not work; the only reason to combine them is price, which is a narrower and more fragile edge.
insights.quote: As a raw diversity play, DeepSeek adds little.
insights.locator: How similar are DeepSeek-V4 Flash and GPT-5.6 Luna?

insights.claim: The combined union of both models covers 106 of 113 DeepSWE tasks (93.8%), but almost all of that reach comes from Luna rather than from complementary strengths.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Multi-model AI coding platforms marketing 'ensemble coverage' should be pressed on whether the second model adds any tasks the first cannot reach.
insights.locator: Their union covers 106 of 113 (93.8%)

insights.claim: The comparison rests on 900 rollouts from published per-trial records (452 DeepSeek, 448 Luna) across all 113 DeepSWE tasks — real long-horizon feature requests from live open-source repos, four trials each, graded pass/fail by a hidden test suite — and the authors warn figures can differ from other public scorecards.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Vendor-run benchmark numbers are not cross-comparable with published leaderboards; treat headline model-comparison claims as run-specific.
insights.quote: Every figure below comes from this run, so it can differ from other public scorecards.
insights.locator: We ran DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 (max) against

insights.claim: The piece is published by Together AI, which simultaneously markets serving DeepSeek-V4 Flash on its own platform as a production first-stage, so the cascade recommendation doubles as a pitch for cheap open-weight inference capacity.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Read the cascade thesis with vendor incentive in mind — the finding favors the publisher's open-weight hosting business.
insights.quote: Serve the cheap first stage at production scale without frontier token prices.
insights.locator: Available now · Open weights
